purpose: Where Council of AI (CSOAI Ltd, UK Companies House 16939677) takes part, and what each entry does and does not prove. One row per body. Every row names its evidence: a public URL a stranger can open, or a dated mailbox record when the only evidence is private (public_evidence: false). scripts/memberships-check.mjs re-fetches every public URL and fails when one stops answering 200 with our name. Participation is not endorsement, a listing is not adoption, a filing is not recognition. Nothing here is a score, a rank, or a mark.
honesty_line: Participation is not endorsement, and a listing is not adoption. Every entry links to its evidence.

Three reasons appear: we hold something weaker than the word would suggest, we are not eligible, or the body has no membership to hold. Each says which. Not listed.

excluded.org: European Commission — General-Purpose AI Code of Practice
excluded.why: The Commission's own text limits signing to providers of general-purpose AI models. Council of AI provides no general-purpose AI model; we measure models other people place on the market. Signing would misdescribe what we are, so we have not applied and will not. This is an eligibility answer, not a backlog item.

Members are nominated by OECD member countries and by stakeholder delegations, which renew or replace their representatives each year. There is no application form and no expression-of-interest route, so there is nothing for us to have applied to. The OECD door that is open to a company is the Catalogue of Tools & Metrics for Trustworthy AI, and that is a submission rather than a membership.

GPAI membership is held by countries, and its work has been integrated with the OECD. There has never been a company membership to apply for, so any claim of GPAI participation by a company is a category error.

The free Associate tier is limited to government bodies, nonprofits and universities. CSOAI Ltd is a private for-profit company and fails that at the first requirement. The tier we could buy starts at USD 15,000 a year at our headcount, less an existing-Linux-Foundation-member discount, and we have not bought it. We do hold Linux Foundation membership at Silver, which is the row above; it is not the same thing.

The IETF has no membership. What is true and checkable is listed above as three mailing-list rows and one Internet-Draft. Three further submissions uploaded on 2026-09-12 were never posted and are not documents on the Datatracker, so they are not participation and are not counted here.

Distinct from C2PA membership, which is listed above with public evidence. A conformance application has been in flight since 2026-08-17 and must be resubmitted on the programme's 0.2 intake form. An application is not a conformance result and nothing about it is claimed on any Council of AI surface.

A full sweep of nicholas@csoai.org across the whole of 2026 — every folder, headers and full-text body search — returns exactly one message containing the word MLCommons, and it is outbound: a note we wrote on 2026-09-17 about a measurement WE published, in which MLCommons AILuminate is one of fifteen organisations we examined. There is no welcome, no invoice, no agreement and no confirmation of any kind. Council of AI is not a member of MLCommons and no row claims otherwise. MLCommons does publish a free Observer tier for organisations of nought to nine employees, which we would qualify for; if we ever apply, the conflict — that we have published a measurement about them — is declared in the application and recorded here.
